title: The Visitor Who Wanted to Stay

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VII: KNOWLEDGE, CONSENT AND SHARED WORK (LCG-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume III concepts (201-300): weather readers and navigators, seed keepers and terrace builders, permission and consent, who leads and who is heard, homes built by many hands, songs for the uncelebrated, and a village writing its own story.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: A newcomer wants to stay but keep their homeland's customs: welcome them as they are, or ask them to follow Isola's ways.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A visitor has asked to stay on Isola for good. (other.He/she) wants to keep (other.his/her) homeland's customs: eating only at night, praying to the moon, wearing (other.his/her) hair in a long braid. (subject) says the village should welcome (other.him/her) as (other.he/she) is. (friend) worries about a newcomer who will not follow the village's ways. What should the village decide?

choices.label: Ask Them to Follow Our Ways

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The village welcomes the newcomer. (other.He/she) eats at night, prays to the moon, and works harder than anyone in the gardens. Within a year, half the village has tried eating at night, and some of them prefer it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) asks the newcomer to follow Isola's ways. The newcomer agrees, unhappily, and stays. But (other.he/she) prays to the moon in secret, alone, on the beach. When (subject) finds out, (subject.he/she) goes and sits with (other.him/her).
